description:
RSRP was consistently strong, ranging between -75.0 dB and -73.0 dB. The average RSRP was -73.2 dB. Uplink modulation and coding (UL_MCS) exhibited two notable drops: it fell to 9 at one interval and to 11 at another; overall UL_MCS ranged from 9.0 to 18.0 with a mean of 15.9. Downlink MCS remained flat at 7.0. Downlink BLER stayed very low, ranging from 0 to 0.06 with a mean of 0.01, while uplink BLER was higher, between 0.023 and 0.17 with a mean of 0.089.

Uplink resource usage (UL_NPRB) was dynamic with several sharp jumps and drops—the largest spike reached 46.1—and overall UL_NPRB ranged from 5.0 to 46.4 with a mean of 24.1. Corresponding UL_SNR varied between 17.6 dB and 26.5 dB with an average of 20.7 dB.

Traffic volume on the uplink (TX_Bytes) was high, spanning 325,113 Bytes to 452,492 Bytes and averaging 436,864.4 Bytes. Downlink throughput (RX_Bytes) was much lower, between 1,689 Bytes and 21,022 Bytes with a mean of 6,523.2 Bytes. The estimated uplink buffer size ranged from 3,235.0 KB to 4,842.1 KB and averaged 3,811.7 KB.

Downlink PRB assignment (PRBs_DL_Current) ranged from 58.0 to 73.1 with a mean of 63.9, and LU PRB assignment (PRBs_UL_Current) was minimal, between 0.05 and 5.1 with a mean of 1.8. DL PRB utilization varied from 54.8% to 69.0% with an average of 60.3%, while UL PRB utilization was very low, between 0.047% and 4.8% with a mean of 1.7%.

Packet counts reflected asymmetric traffic: uplink packets ranged from 20 to 189 with a mean of 76.3, while downlink packet counts experienced sudden large spikes up to 1,926 and overall ranged from 0 to 1,926 with a mean of 282.3. Protocol usage was overwhelmingly TCP: UL traffic was TCP 100.00% of the time, and DL traffic was TCP for 82.81% of timestamps.

The RSRP is stable at −73.0 dB, indicating a consistent signal strength, so the issue isn't related to signal loss or fluctuation. Moving on to MCS values, DL MCS is constant at 7 while UL MCS drops by 6 points (from 15 to 9). This suggests a problem in the uplink that isn't impacting the downlink significantly. 

Next, the UL BLER averages 0.1, which is relatively high compared to the DL BLER average of 0.0083. High BLER in UL indicates a higher rate of transmission errors. However, the UL SNR (18.3–24.3 dB, averaging 20.2 dB) doesn't show major degradation, so it's unlikely the issue is due to noise or weak signal.

Looking at PRB utilization, the DL PRBs are heavily used (53.8–63.8%, avg. 60.3%), which is expected for steady downlink traffic. This mismatch implies that the system is unable to allocate sufficient UL resources to clear the buffer, possibly due to interference or deliberate blocking of uplink communications. 

Additionally, the large DL packet bursts (peaks of 1,683 and 1,706 packets) suggest contention for resources, but the UL side shows no corresponding increase in PRB allocation. The uplink packet count is also low (32–131, avg. 71.1), despite the buffer growing, which further supports the idea of constrained uplink capacity.

Putting it all together, the combination of stable signal metrics (RSRP, SNR), high UL BLER, low UL PRB utilization, and a growing buffer despite regular uplink traffic points to an intentional or external interference that's disrupting the uplink without significantly affecting the downlink. 

Therefore, this pattern is consistent with 'jamming'.

description:

UL SNR varied between 18.1 dB and 25.4 dB; its mean is 20.2 dB. Uplink NPRBs allocated ranged from 11.1 to 39.9 with a mean of 20.9. Downlink PRBs in use ranged from 58.0 to 68.1 with a mean of 63.8.

DL BLER spanned 0.00013 to 0.063 with a mean of 0.0081, while UL BLER ranged 0.028 to 0.18 with a mean of 0.083. DL PRB utilization varied between 54.8% and 64.3% (mean 60.2%), whereas UL PRB utilization stayed very low between 0.15% and 3.5% (mean 1.3%). Current UL PRBs observed were between 0.16 and 3.7 (mean 1.4).

Traffic volumes were heavily downlink-dominated: TX_Bytes (uplink) ranged 390,379 to 453,340 Bytes with a mean of 437,608.9 Bytes; RX_Bytes (downlink) ranged 3,515 to 10,525 Bytes with a mean of 5,087.7 Bytes. The estimated uplink transmit buffer varied from 633.1 to 1,229.2 Kilobytes, mean 887.9 KB. Packet counts: UL packets ranged 36 to 105 (mean 74.0); DL packets ranged 0 to 910 (mean 283.4).

Protocol usage was overwhelmingly TCP: UL was TCP 100.00%, DL was TCP for 92.97% of timestamps (UDP absent). Overall, the link presents stable downlink signal power and modest SNR with occasional UL MCS drops, low UL PRB usage and utilization, low-to-moderate BLERs, and traffic dominated by downlink packet volume and TCP.
